acceptance_criteria.criterion: When a workspace has health issues, the alert section is visible with per-issue rows and fix buttons.
When a workspace is healthy, no alert section is rendered.
Clicking "Regenerate File" calls api.workspaces.regenerateFile(), shows a success toast, and re-fetches health.
Clicking the setup fix button calls api.workspaces.setup(), shows a success toast, and re-fetches health.
Health is re-fetched on manual refresh ("Refresh Now") and automatic poll.
The "Retry Setup" block no longer fires for repos with missing .git/ directories (now covered by health alerts).
The "Retry Setup" block still fires for repos with .git/ present but no status data (transient polling-lag case).
The view's cleanup function properly handles any new intervals or listeners.

summary: Added `buildHealthAlertSection()` module-level function that renders a `.health-alert` card with per-issue rows and fix buttons (`Regenerate File` for `regenerate-workspace-file`, `Fix Setup` for `setup-workspace`).
Extended `renderWorkspaceDetail` Promise.all to fetch health alongside existing data (5th slot, `.catch(() => null)` guard).
Added `healthContainerEl` div (always in DOM between header and toolbar) and `currentHealthReport` variable.
Added `renderHealthSection(report)` function that updates `currentHealthReport` and repopulates `healthContainerEl` via `buildHealthAlertSection`.
Added `fetchAndRenderHealth()` async function used by fix buttons to re-fetch health after a fix action.

Updated `doPoll` and `doRefresh` to fetch health in parallel with status via `Promise.all`; `renderHealthSection` is called before `updateMissingReposRow` so `currentHealthReport` is current when the retry row is re-evaluated.
Updated `updateMissingReposRow` to compute `notClonedIds` from `currentHealthReport` and exclude those repos from the missing-count — satisfying the narrowed Retry Setup behaviour (AC6/AC7).
Updated initial DOM assembly `missingRepos` filter to apply the same `notClonedRepoIds` exclusion.
All 699 existing tests pass.

comments.note: In `buildHealthAlertSection`, the `btn` variable is declared once outside the if/else branches but never used in the fallthrough (unknown `fixAction`) path. Each branch already creates its own `btn` locally — the outer declaration is dead code. Minor cleanup opportunity.

The `onSetup` callback inside `renderHealthSection` calls `doRefresh()` (fire-and-forget) then `fetchAndRenderHealth()` in sequence. Because `doRefresh` also fetches health internally, this results in two concurrent health fetches after a setup fix; the last-writer-wins on `currentHealthReport`. Harmless currently, but worth noting if health checks become expensive.

No observations beyond the above — workspace-detail.js code in the touched areas is well-structured, follows established patterns, and the new helpers integrate cleanly with the existing polling/refresh machinery.

comments.note: onSetup callback in renderHealthSection calls doRefresh() then fetchAndRenderHealth() in sequence (gui/public/js/views/workspace-detail.js ~line 855). Because doRefresh() also fetches health internally via Promise.all, this produces two concurrent health fetches after a setup fix action. Both resolve to the same endpoint; last-writer-wins on currentHealthReport is harmless. If health checks become expensive, consolidating to a single fetch path (e.g. awaiting doRefresh() and skipping the separate fetchAndRenderHealth call) would be cleaner.

summary: Reviewed gui/public/js/views/workspace-detail.js line-by-line. All four review dimensions pass cleanly — Maintainability, Best Practices, Performance, and Future Context.
buildHealthAlertSection: callback injection pattern is the correct architectural choice. Decouples the section-builder from the outer closure, making it independently testable. JSDoc is accurate.

renderHealthSection + fetchAndRenderHealth: well-focused, single-responsibility. container.isConnected guard is correctly placed. finally blocks used consistently for button state reset across all fix buttons.

currentHealthReport mutable closure variable: clearly documented inline, updated before updateMissingReposRow calls (correct ordering in doPoll/doRefresh ensures notClonedIds exclusion is always based on latest health data).

notClonedRepoIds set is computed twice (DOM assembly from initial healthReport, updateMissingReposRow from currentHealthReport) — two separate scopes with different data sources; this duplication is intentional and acceptable.

Known double-fetch on onSetup (doRefresh fire-and-forget + fetchAndRenderHealth): confirmed harmless. btn reference goes stale after renderHealthSection clears healthContainerEl.innerHTML, but the finally block no-ops cleanly on a detached element. No UX regression.
No Fix-Forward changes applied. No blocking issues found. Two documentation-forward items recorded for the Documentation agent.

comments.note: onSetup callback (renderHealthSection closure, ~line 855): doRefresh() is called without await, then fetchAndRenderHealth() follows. Both run concurrently — doRefresh also fetches health internally via Promise.all. The race is harmless (last-writer-wins on currentHealthReport), but a future optimization path would be to await doRefresh() and drop the separate fetchAndRenderHealth() call to consolidate to a single health fetch. Not a blocking issue at current scale.
